input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 (the first of two clauses numbered 7.2) conditions Customer's engagement of any other provider on disclosing and matching for Vendor any more favourable offer it receives. That is a de facto right of first refusal and functions as an exclusivity restraint on our freedom to source: it is unlimited in product category, unlimited in duration (the full term), and has no automatic exit on Vendor's failure to meet service levels or delivery dates, so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. The only other "exclusive" references (§§ 13.1, 14.2, 19.4, 21.4, 28.1-28.2, 30.2) concern licence scope, remedies, and jurisdiction, not exclusive dealing. Smallest edit to reach the preferred position is deletion of p0026; the substantive payment-terms 7.2 (p0027) is unaffected. Flagged here as a restrictive covenant on sourcing rather than as an MFN pricing term.

proposal.summary: Delete the disclose-and-match precondition on Customer engaging another provider
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the requirement to disclose and match third-party offers before engaging another provider, as it operates as a de facto exclusivity/right of first refusal on our sourcing for the full term with no performance-based exit. Our playbook position is that Vendor is a non-exclusive provider, consistent with Section 12.3.
